When Apple unveiled the Apple Watch Series 12, two features stood out the most: the all-new Siri Recap feature, and a significantly improved heart rate monitor. While those two features were among the reasons I purchased the new Apple Watch, I discovered there was far more that surprised me.

Battery and Charging

Although Apple's website does not list any additional battery life improvement for the Apple Watch Series 12 over the Series 11, the battery does feel noticeably more durable. As I've written before, prior to using the Apple Watch Series 12, I was a WHOOP user, and although I always kept my Apple Watch, I never used it to track sleep.

After the launch event, I decided to give Apple Watch's sleep tracking a try. That said, on my Series 11, juggling both sleep tracking and charging was a bit of a hassle. After wearing the watch all day, I had to charge it before bed, and then charge it again after waking up in the morning.

With the Series 12, however, things are different. Its battery is enough to last an entire day plus a whole night, and now I only need to charge it after I get up. The Apple Watch Series 12 also charges considerably faster, making this part much less of a hassle. According to Apple's data, a 15-minute charge provides up to 12 hours of use.

I suspect the brand-new S11 chip — derived from the A20 Pro's 2nm design — is the primary reason for the significantly extended battery life. Regardless of the reason, no longer worrying about battery for sleep tracking on the Apple Watch Series 12 is truly fantastic. Another major advantage of the S11 chip? The Apple Watch Series 12 is noticeably faster, especially when using Siri.

Exclusive Software Features

On the Series 12, Apple has finally added an official step counter as a watch face complication, which I enjoy viewing in the Smart Stack. Will this feature be rolled out to older Apple Watch models? Quite possibly. After all, Apple hasn't been unfamiliar with counting steps before. The Apple Watch Series 12 certainly counts steps more accurately, but given that the relevant data already exists, I think Apple should have simply added this complication. Either way, it's nice to have this feature on the Series 12.

Another excellent new feature is the all-new Readiness app, which tells you how you're doing today based on last night's sleep, the previous day's activity, and your vital signs. This is similar to WHOOP's recovery score, and I'm of course delighted to see Apple add this feature to the Apple Watch. Unfortunately, this feature is exclusive to the Series 12, but I also understand why Apple wouldn't want to calculate this metric with less accurate data.

Summary

All in all, the Apple Watch Series 12 is a rather impressive upgrade. This is entirely an 'S' year update, but if what you care about is actual functional improvements to the Apple Watch rather than just cosmetic changes, I'd say this is potentially one of the most significant year-over-year upgrades since the Apple Watch Series 4.

Compared with the Series 10 and 11, the bezels are indeed slightly thicker. For users with dark watch face backgrounds, I personally don't notice it too much — but I hope Apple can improve this further in the next generation.

One final thing worth mentioning: the Apple Watch Series 12 comes equipped with Ceramic Shield 2 for the aluminium models, making it far more scratch-resistant than older Apple Watch models. I haven't owned it long enough to truly test this, but so far, my Apple Watch still looks flawless.
